verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents running the complete platform on your own infrastructure with full control over your data. It provides Docker and Kubernetes/Helm deployment paths, and a self-hosted Edge Proxy keeps flag evaluation close to your servers. A community user also evaluated it as a self-hosted tool. However, the evidence never explicitly says the self-hostable distribution is open-source or under what license, and it does not show that evaluation data stays entirely on-prem; missing for 10: an explicit open-source license statement for the full self-hosted distribution, and explicit documentation that evaluation and analytics data remain on user infrastructure.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can self-host the full flag platform from an open-source distribution, keeping evaluation data on my infrastructure

citations.quote: Self-hosting Flagsmith allows you to run the complete Flagsmith platform within your own infrastructure, giving you full control over your data, security policies, and deployment environment.
Kubernetes and OpenShift: Full Kubernetes deployment with Helm charts and operators
You can use Docker to set up an entire Flagsmith Feature Flag environment locally
The Flagsmith Edge Proxy is a service that you host yourself, that allows you to run an instance of the Flagsmith Engine close to your servers.
